name: Telegram
one_liner: Telegram provides the Bot API (an HTTP-based interface for building bots) and the Telegram API/TDLib (for building custom clients using the MTProto protocol).

auth.notes: The Bot API is accessed via an HTTPS interface (tokens managed via @BotFather), while the Telegram API uses an api_id and api_hash for MTProto-based authorization.

access.notes: Developers can obtain api_id and api_hash by logging into the Telegram core website (my.telegram.org) and filling out a form, or create bots via the @BotFather bot.

api_surface.notes: The Bot API is HTTP-based and supports webhooks for processing updates. The Telegram API uses the MTProto protocol and is supported by the TDLib library, which is compatible with multiple platforms and languages.

mcp.notes: The provided text does not mention the Model Context Protocol (MCP).

buildability.reasoning: Access to credentials (api_id/hash and bot tokens) is entirely self-serve via the Telegram core site or @BotFather. The APIs are extensively documented, and official libraries like TDLib facilitate development across multiple platforms.

evidence.claim: The Bot API is an HTTP-based interface created for developers building bots for Telegram.
Developers can obtain an api_id and api_hash by logging into my.telegram.org and filling out the API development tools form.
Telegram supports processing bot updates via webhooks (setWebhook).
TDLib is a tool for third-party developers that makes it easy to build fast, secure and feature-rich Telegram apps and is compatible with virtually any programming language.
Authorization for the Telegram API requires api_id and api_hash parameters.

name: Stripe
one_liner: A REST-based payments platform that provides a suite of APIs and SDKs for processing payments, managing subscriptions, and financial operations using API key authentication.

auth.notes: Stripe uses API keys (secret, restricted, or publishable) for authentication, typically passed via HTTP Basic Auth as the username. Bearer token authentication is also supported for cross-origin requests.

access.notes: Users can sign up for an account and obtain API keys immediately via the dashboard without manual approval.

api_surface.notes: The API is REST-based and supports webhooks and multiple official SDKs for server-side, web, and mobile platforms.

mcp.notes: Model Context Protocol is listed as a feature under AI tools and Agent plugins, but the provided text contains no substantive description of the capability.

buildability.reasoning: Stripe provides self-serve account registration with immediate access to API keys, comprehensive REST documentation, and official SDKs for many languages.

evidence.claim: The Stripe API is organized around REST and uses API keys for authentication.
Users can sign up and create a Stripe account.
Stripe creates API keys upon account signup and lists Model Context Protocol as a feature.
Stripe provides official SDKs for Ruby, Python, Go, Java, Node, PHP, .NET, iOS, Android, and React Native.

name: DealCloud
one_liner: DealCloud is an AI-powered deal and relationship intelligence platform for professional firms, offering a REST API and SDKs for integration.

auth.notes: OAuth2 Client Credentials is described as the most common method for API integrations. The platform also supports API keys, Basic Auth, JWT, and enterprise identity providers like Microsoft Entra ID and Okta.

access.notes: Obtaining credentials requires an existing DealCloud environment (site URL) and client credentials. The public website directs prospective users to schedule a demo.

api_surface.notes: The documentation provides a dedicated Intapp REST Client and SDKs for Python and C#.

mcp.notes: The provided text contains no mention of Model Context Protocol (MCP).

buildability.reasoning: The API is well-documented with multiple SDKs and clear authentication patterns (OAuth2, API Key). However, access is gated, requiring a pre-existing DealCloud environment and credentials obtained through sales or account management.

evidence.claim: OAuth2 Client Credentials is the most common authentication method for API integrations, with support for API keys, Basic Auth, and JWT.
The Python SDK requires a site URL, client ID, and client secret to instantiate the client.
The product website directs users to 'Schedule a demo' rather than providing self-serve sign-up.
The platform provides a REST Client and SDKs for Python and C#.
